haiku-low.q1: The old engine computes, writes the ledger and charges. The new engine's invoices go only to the shadow store, never charged or ledgered.
haiku-low.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine computes into the shadow store only and never charges.
haiku-low.q3: Gate 1: 7 consecutive days with mismatch rate under 0.1% and at least 5,000 invoices compared. A person moves it; the rollout tool checks the gate.
haiku-low.q4: The billing monitor, when the new engine's charge failure rate exceeds 2% in any 10-minute window, in both or new_only. On-call can also start one manually from shadow, both or new_only.
haiku-low.q5: Every rollback ends at old_only after all remaining steps and deleting the rollback record. Before the new engine returns, the rollout must pass shadow again and gates reset.
haiku-low.q6: From day 35 in new_only, because the usage event log keeps only 35 days, so catch_up cannot find the events. The tool then refuses and a person is alerted.
haiku-low.q7: Workers read the billing_mode flag from the config service. How fast they notice is NOT STATED. Invoices due during the pause are held, not dropped, and reconcile handles them.
haiku-low.q8: Evidence is in comparison_results, and the rollout tool computes the gate numbers itself. It refuses a forward move if the gate is unmet or a rollback record exists. Finance sign-off location is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q9: The billing monitor measures the new engine's charge failure rate over any 10-minute window. Above 2%, it starts a rollback by calling the rollout tool.
haiku-low.q10: Charges falling due are held, not dropped, while charging is paused. Reconcile makes them during the rollback, the only charging then; normal charging resumes at resume_charging.
haiku-low.q11: Each charge first checks for an existing charge record and charges only if none exists. Reconcile does the same check. Whether the record is on the ledger is not verified.
haiku-low.q12: The tool retries the same step, which is safe. If retries keep failing, the rollback stays in progress with charging paused until a person steps in. A crash is resumed from the recorded step.

sonnet.q1: The old engine computes, writes the ledger and charges. The new engine's invoices go to the shadow store only.
sonnet.q2: The new engine writes the ledger and charges. The old engine computes into the shadow store only, to stay current, and never charges.
sonnet.q3: Gate 1 must be met: 7 consecutive days with a mismatch rate under 0.1% and at least 5,000 invoices compared. A person makes the move, using the rollout tool. The tool computes the gate itself from comparison_results and refuses if it is not met.
sonnet.q4: The billing monitor starts one when the new engine's charge failure rate is above 2% over any 10-minute window. This applies in both and new_only, before day 35 in new_only. It does not apply in shadow.
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only. After any rollback the gates reset: the rollout must go through shadow again and the 7-day count starts over, passing gate 1 and then gate 2.
sonnet.q6: It stops from day 35 in new_only, counted from mode_entered_at. The usage event log keeps events only 35 days, so catch_up can no longer find them.
sonnet.q7: Workers read the billing_mode flag from the config service. How quickly they notice a change is not known. For an invoice in process at that moment, NOT STATED. The document says only that during a rollback charging_paused stops a worker that has not yet seen the change from charging.
sonnet.q8: Gate evidence is in comparison_results, written by the nightly comparison job. Finance sign-off for gate 2 is kept somewhere not known. The rollout tool stops early promotion: it reads comparison_results, computes the gate numbers itself and refuses to advance if the gate is not met. It also refuses if a rollback record exists.
sonnet.q9: The billing monitor. It measures the new engine's charge failure rate, with a threshold of above 2% over any 10-minute window in both or new_only. When the condition is met it starts a rollback by calling the rollout tool. From day 35 in new_only or after decommissioning, no rollback starts and a person is alerted.
sonnet.q10: Charging is paused, so neither engine charges. Invoices that fall due are held, not dropped. Reconcile makes the charges, and only reconcile charges during a rollback. It charges only if no charge record exists. After resume_charging the old engine's normal run charges periods as they fall due.
sonnet.q11: The charge record. The new engine's successful charge wrote one on the ledger, and reconcile charges only if no charge record exists. Every charge first checks this.
sonnet.q12: Charging stays paused because charging_paused is still set, and the rollback record keeps the progress. The tool retries the same step, which is safe because reconcile checks the charge record. If retries keep failing, the rollback stays in progress with charging paused, nobody is charged twice, and a person must step in. If the tool crashes, a person or the monitor firing again runs it and it resumes at the recorded step.
